n851e8a91fae.s: Which of the following pairs about the Human Development Index is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Health – Included as an HDI dimension
Education – Included as an HDI dimension
Inequality – A criticism: not reflected in the HDI
Sustainability – Included as an HDI dimension
n851e8a91fae.x: The HDI includes health and education; one of its criticisms is that it ignores sustainability, along with inequality, gender and political freedom.

ne7649606167.s: Among the Rayalaseema districts (13-district set), which had the lowest population density?
ne7649606167.x: In Rayalaseema, YSR Kadapa had the lowest density, while Kurnool had the highest child share.

new.s: In Amartya Sen's capability approach, capabilities are described as:
o: Substantive freedoms to lead lives people value
Rise in per capita national income
Fixed universal list of basic needs
new.x: Sen defined capabilities as substantive freedoms to lead the lives people value and avoided a fixed universal list.

new.s: Who is the Pakistani economist who conceived the Human Development Report?
new.x: Mahbub ul Haq, a Pakistani economist, conceived the HDR, which he co-conceived with Amartya Sen.

new.s: What are the goalposts used for life expectancy at birth in the HDI?
new.x: The health dimension uses life expectancy at birth with goalposts of 20 and 85 years.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the HDI knowledge dimension:
1. Mean years of schooling is measured for adults aged 25 and above.
2. Expected years of schooling has a goalpost of 0–18 years.
3. Adult literacy rate is still one of its indicators.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: MYS (adults 25+, goalpost 0–15) and EYS (0–18) measure knowledge; literacy was replaced by them in 2010.

new.s: Which neighbouring country shared India's rank of 130 in the HDR 2025?
new.x: Bangladesh shares rank 130 with India; Sri Lanka (89) and Bhutan (125) are ahead and Nepal (145) is below.

new.s: In the HDR 2025, Sri Lanka's HDI rank was:
new.x: Sri Lanka ranked 89, ahead of India (130); China was 78 and Nepal 145.

new.s: Which country ranked first in the Human Development Report 2025?
new.x: Iceland topped the HDR 2025 with an HDI of 0.972; South Sudan was last (193rd).

new.s: Which country has the highest life expectancy as per the HDR 2025?
new.x: Japan has the highest life expectancy, while Iceland ranked first overall.

new.s: Which country was ranked last (193rd) in the HDR 2025?
new.x: South Sudan was ranked last, 193rd, in the HDR 2025.

new.s: Which index is described as HDI discounted for inequality?
new.x: The IHDI discounts the HDI for inequality; the gap between HDI and IHDI is the loss due to inequality.

new.s: The Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI), a pre-HDI measure, used which indicators?
new.x: The PQLI combined literacy, infant mortality and life expectancy before the HDI was introduced.

new.s: According to NITI Aayog (January 2024), multidimensional poverty in India fell from 29.17% in 2013-14 to:
new.x: NITI Aayog reported a fall from 29.17% to 11.28%, with 24.82 crore people moving out of poverty.

new.s: Which State recorded the biggest fall in the number of multidimensionally poor (2013-14 to 2022-23)?
new.x: Uttar Pradesh saw the biggest fall (5.94 crore), followed by Bihar and Madhya Pradesh.

new.s: The first National Human Development Report of India (2001) was prepared by:
new.x: The first NHDR (2001) was brought out by the Planning Commission and released on 23 April 2002; Kerala was top.

new.s: Which State topped the first National Human Development Report of India?
new.x: Kerala was ranked top in the first NHDR (2001).

new.s: Which two States have a state HDI above 0.86 in the sub-national series?
new.x: Kerala and Goa are above 0.86, while Bihar is lowest at 0.650.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh's multidimensional poverty headcount ratio (6.06%) compares with a national figure of:
new.x: AP's headcount of 6.06% is well below the national 14.96%; AP's MPI halved from 0.053 to 0.025.

new.s: The population density of undivided Andhra Pradesh in 2011 was:
new.x: 308 was undivided AP's density; residual AP's is 304 and India's 382.

new.s: The population density of Andhra Pradesh in 2001 was:
Which district had the highest population density among the 13 districts of Andhra Pradesh in 2011?
new.x: Krishna (518 per sq km) was the densest of the 13 districts; YSR Kadapa was the least dense.

new.s: Which was the least populous district of Andhra Pradesh among the 13 districts in Census 2011?
new.x: Vizianagaram (about 23.4 lakh) was the least populous; East Godavari was the most populous.

new.s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh was the most rural in 2011 (only 16.16% urban)?
new.x: Srikakulam was the most rural district; Visakhapatnam (47.45%) was the most urban.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Andhra Pradesh's 28-district structure (2025)?
o: SPSR Nellore is the most populous district
Polavaram is the least populous district
East Godavari has the lowest density
new.x: Polavaram (54 per sq km) has the lowest density in the 28-district set; East Godavari was the most populous of the 13 districts in 2011.

new.s: Which decade recorded the highest decadal population growth in Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: AP's highest decadal growth was 21.13% in 1981–91.

new.s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh grew fastest during 2001–11?
new.x: Kurnool grew fastest (about 14.7%) and West Godavari slowest (about 3.5%) in 2001–11.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh's population growth during 2001–11 was:
new.x: AP grew 9.21% in 2001–11, about half India's 17.7%.

new.s: What is the crude death rate (SRS) of Andhra Pradesh compared with India's 6.4?
new.x: AP's CDR is 6.9, higher than India's 6.4, even though its birth rate is lower.

new.s: What incentive did the AP Chief Minister announce in May 2026 for a third child?
new.x: Rs 30,000 for the 3rd child and Rs 40,000 for the 4th, under the 'Pillale Sampada' idea.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh's population policy in 2026:
1. The two-child cap for local body elections was removed.
2. The Draft Population Management Policy aims to raise TFR from 1.5 to 2.1.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The two-child cap was removed on 12 Feb 2026 and the draft policy of 5 Mar 2026 aims to raise TFR from 1.5 to 2.1.

new.s: The rise of households faster than population in Andhra Pradesh indicates a shift towards:
new.x: Households grew faster than population, showing a shift to nuclear families (52.1% rural, 52.3% urban in 2011).

new.s: About what share of Andhra Pradesh's population lived in Rayalaseema (13-district set)?
new.x: Rayalaseema had about 31%, the rest of Coastal Andhra about 50% and Uttarandhra about 19%.

new.s: According to Census 2011, the sex ratio of Andhra Pradesh was higher than India's 943 by:
new.x: AP's 997 is 54 above India's 943.

new.s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh had the highest sex ratio in Census 2011 (13-district map)?
new.x: Vizianagaram had the highest sex ratio, followed by Srikakulam; Anantapuramu had the lowest (977).

new.s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh had the lowest sex ratio (977) in Census 2011?
new.x: Anantapuramu, in Rayalaseema, had the lowest sex ratio of 977.

new.s: As per NFHS-5, the sex ratio at birth in Andhra Pradesh was:
new.x: AP's sex ratio at birth rose from 914 (NFHS-4) to 934 (NFHS-5); India's NFHS-5 figure was 929.

new.s: The child sex ratio (0–6) of undivided Andhra Pradesh in 2011 was:
new.x: It fell to 939 from 961 in 2001, though still above India's 919.

new.s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh had the highest child sex ratio (968) in 2011?
new.x: East Godavari recorded the highest district child sex ratio of 968 in 2011.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh between 2001 and 2011:
1. The overall sex ratio rose from 983 to 997.
2. The child sex ratio rose from 939 to 961.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The overall sex ratio rose (983 to 997) while the child sex ratio fell from 961 to 939.

new.s: What was the literacy rate of Andhra Pradesh in Census 2011?
new.x: AP's literacy was 67.35% (male 74.77%, female 59.96%).

new.s: The female literacy rate of Andhra Pradesh in Census 2011 was:
new.x: Female literacy was 59.96% against male 74.77%, a gap of about 15 points.

new.s: Which was the most literate district among the 13 districts of Andhra Pradesh in Census 2011?
new.x: West Godavari (74.63%) was the most literate; Vizianagaram (58.89%) the least on the 13-district map.

new.s: The literacy rate of Scheduled Tribes in Andhra Pradesh is:
new.x: ST literacy is 48.8% against the State's 67.35%; 44.67% is ASR district's rate.

new.s: Which district was the least literate on the 13-district map of Andhra Pradesh (2011)?
new.x: Vizianagaram (58.89%) was least literate among the 13 districts; ASR is lowest on the new 26/28 map.

new.s: Which was the first Union Territory declared fully literate?
new.x: Ladakh (2024) was the first fully literate UT; Mizoram (2025) the first State.

new.s: Under ULLAS, an area is declared fully literate when literacy among those aged 15+ reaches:
new.x: The fully literate benchmark is 95%+ literacy among people aged 15 and above, not 100%.

new.s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh has the highest share of agricultural labourers?
new.x: West Godavari, a delta paddy district, has the highest share of agricultural labourers.

new.s: In Andhra Pradesh (2011), agricultural labourers were roughly how many times the cultivators?
new.x: Agricultural labourers were the largest worker category, almost three times cultivators.

new.s: In undivided Andhra Pradesh, the share of cultivators among main workers fell between 2001 and 2011 from 22.52% to:
new.x: Cultivators fell from 22.52% to 16.47% while agricultural labourers rose from 39.63% to about 43%.

new.s: As per PLFS 2023-24, what share of Andhra Pradesh's workers is in agriculture?
new.x: PLFS 2023-24 puts AP's agriculture share at 45.6%; 54.6% is India's Census 2011 figure.

new.s: The overall work participation rate of undivided Andhra Pradesh in 2011 was about:
new.x: Undivided AP's overall WPR in 2011 was about 46.6%.

new.s: The female main-worker participation rate in Andhra Pradesh in 2011 was:
new.x: Female main-worker participation rose to 35.04% in 2011 from 33.01% in 2001.

new.s: The PCPNDT Act, which tackles son preference and sex-selective abortion, was enacted in:
new.x: The PCPNDT Act dates from 1994; in June 2026 the Supreme Court flagged persisting son preference under it.
